abstract: Randomly breaking connections in a graph alters its transport properties, a model used to describe percolation. In the case of quantum walks, dynamic percolation graphs represent a special type of imperfections, where the connections appear and disappear randomly in each step during the time evolution. The resulting open system dynamics is hard to treat numerically in general. We shortly review the literature on this problem. We then present our method to solve the evolution on finite percolation graphs in the long time limit, applying the asymptotic methods concerning random unitary maps. We work out the case of one dimensional chains in detail and provide a concrete, step by step numerical example in order to give more insight into the possible asymptotic behavior. The results about the case of the two-dimensional integer lattice are summarized, focusing on the Grover type coin operator.

specification.problem: Describe the long-time asymptotic dynamics of a discrete-time quantum walk on finite dynamic percolation graphs, where edges appear and disappear randomly at each step. The evolution is a random unitary map, and the long-time limit is analyzed with asymptotic methods for such maps. The 1D chain is treated in detail, and the 2D integer lattice with a Grover coin is summarized.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the random-unitary-map formulation and a tiny finite example, such as a short 1D chain. It does not reproduce the paper's specific results, numerical example values, or 2D lattice findings.

equations.label: Random unitary map
equations.description: Averaged one-step evolution over random edge configurations, with a fresh configuration drawn independently each step.
equations.abstract_quote: applying the asymptotic methods concerning random unitary maps
equations.justification: The abstract names random unitary maps as the framework. The explicit form is standard background and assumes independent configurations per step.
assumptions: Edge configurations are i.i.d. across steps

equations.label: Long-time evolution
equations.description: Asymptotics of the averaged state. In general the limit may be a periodic or oscillating asymptotic behavior rather than a single fixed point.
equations.abstract_quote: solve the evolution on finite percolation graphs in the long time limit
equations.justification: Directly follows from the stated long-time evolution goal. The limit may not exist in general.
assumptions: Limit taken along a suitable subsequence if the dynamics is periodic

specification.initial_state: Assumed finite instance: a localized walker with an arbitrary coin state, rho_0 = |x_0,c_0><x_0,c_0|, on a short 1D chain.

steps.description: Prepare the initial coin-position state rho_0.
At each time step, draw an independent edge configuration omega with probability p_omega.
Apply the coin operator and the conditional shift U_omega, which is blocked on missing edges. Averaging over omega gives the channel Phi.
Repeat for t steps and analyze the asymptotic behavior of Phi^t.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after t steps, measure the walker in the position basis (coin traced out) to get P_t(x)=sum_c <x,c|rho_t|x,c>. Repeat over many runs and edge-configuration samples. The averaged state rho_t is the ensemble average, so the statistics match Phi^t(rho_0).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_t(x) from outcome frequencies for several large t. Compare with the asymptotic distribution from rho_infinity, or with its periodic or time-averaged version if the limit oscillates. Check convergence, for example by total variation distance between successive t.
assumptions: Independent identically distributed edge configurations per step
Coin dimension 2 for the 1D chain is assumed
Shift is blocked on missing edges (assumed convention)
Position-basis measurement is assumed; the abstract does not specify a measurement
